lessons.title: Be: am, is and are
objectives: Use am, is and are with the right subject.
Make negative sentences and questions with be.
Distinguish a description from an action verb.
Complete a gap with the missing phrase only.

explanation.en: The verb be connects a person or thing to a name, feeling, place or description. Use I am, he/she/it is, and you/we/they are. In a negative, add not: I am not, she is not (isn't), they are not (aren't). For questions, move be before the subject: Is she ready? Are they in the library? Do not add do/does to questions with be. In a gap-fill, keep the subject already printed.
explanation.vi: Động từ be: I am; he/she/it is; you/we/they are. Phủ định thêm not, câu hỏi đảo am/is/are lên trước chủ ngữ. Điền đúng phần còn thiếu, không viết lại chủ ngữ.

examples: FORM · I am eleven. She is my sister. They are students.
NEGATIVE · He isn't late. We aren't tired.
QUESTION · Are you ready? Yes, I am.
MEANING · 'She is happy' describes a feeling. 'She plays' uses an action verb.
GAP FORMAT · The books ___ on the desk. → are.

activities.prompt: Complete: My cousins ___ at the sports club.

feedback.explanation_en: Cousins is plural; they are at the club. 'Is' agrees with one person or thing.

activities.prompt: Which sentence is correct?

feedback.explanation_en: Use I am; never I is or I are.

activities.prompt: Complete: The library ___ open today.

feedback.explanation_en: The library is one place. Use is, without repeating 'The library'.

activities.prompt: Which is the correct question?

feedback.explanation_en: With be, place is before she. Do not add does.

activities.prompt: Complete: We ___ (not / be) late.

feedback.explanation_en: We takes are; the negative is are not or aren't. Type only the missing phrase.

activities.prompt: Choose the correct reply: Are you hungry?

feedback.explanation_en: The short affirmative answer is Yes, I am. A contracted Yes, I'm is not used as this short answer.

activities.prompt: Which sentence describes a place correctly?

options.text: The science books are on the shelf.
The science books is on the shelf.
The science books am on the shelf.
The science books be on the shelf.

feedback.explanation_en: Books is plural, so are is required.

activities.prompt: Complete: ___ (your teacher / be) here?

feedback.explanation_en: The question starts with Is, followed by the singular subject your teacher.

activities.prompt: Choose the correct negative sentence.

feedback.explanation_en: With be, use isn't, rather than doesn't be. She takes is.

activities.prompt: Complete: I ___ excited about the trip.

feedback.explanation_en: The subject I takes am. Type only am; writing I again would repeat the subject already printed.

lessons.title: Pronouns and possessive adjectives
objectives: Use I, you, he, she, it, we and they as subjects.
Distinguish my, your, his, her, its, our and their before a noun.
Choose a pronoun using meaning and number.
Avoid confusing he/his and they/their.

explanation.en: A subject pronoun replaces the person or thing doing the action: Lan is my friend. She is kind. A possessive adjective comes before a noun to show whose thing it is: her bag, their school, our classroom. Use it/its for a thing and they/their for more than one person. 'It's' means 'it is'; 'its' shows possession. Before answering, ask: Do I need a subject or a word describing ownership?
explanation.vi: Đại từ chủ ngữ đứng thay người/vật: I, you, he, she, it, we, they. Tính từ sở hữu đứng trước danh từ: my, your, his, her, its, our, their. 'Its' khác 'it's' (= it is).

examples: SUBJECT · Minh is my brother. He likes drawing.
OWNERSHIP · Minh has a pencil. His pencil is blue.
PLURAL · Mai and I are classmates. We study together.
CONTRAST · The students have books. They open their books.
COMMON ERROR · It's raining (= it is raining), but the dog wags its tail.

activities.prompt: Linh is my sister. ___ is in class six.

feedback.explanation_en: The phrase my sister identifies one girl, so the subject pronoun is She.

activities.prompt: My brother has a bike. ___ bike is red.

feedback.explanation_en: A word before bike must show ownership: his.

activities.prompt: Complete: Nam and I are friends. ___ walk to school together.

feedback.explanation_en: Nam and I is a group including the speaker: we.

activities.prompt: Choose the sentence with a possessive adjective.

feedback.explanation_en: Our comes before neighbours and tells you whose neighbours they are.

activities.prompt: Complete: Mai and Lan bring ___ notebooks.

feedback.explanation_en: Two named students take their before the plural noun notebooks.

activities.prompt: The cat is cleaning ___ paws.

feedback.explanation_en: Its shows possession. It's means it is, which would not fit before paws here.

activities.prompt: Which sentence correctly replaces 'My parents'?

feedback.explanation_en: Parents is plural; use they with work.

activities.prompt: Complete: This is my sister. ___ name is An.

feedback.explanation_en: Before the noun name, use the possessive adjective her.

activities.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.

feedback.explanation_en: We is the subject; our shows that the classroom belongs to us.

activities.prompt: Complete: This is my new phone. ___ is small.

feedback.explanation_en: The second sentence needs a subject pronoun for one object: it.

lessons.title: Present simple: everyday routines
objectives: Describe repeated habits using the present simple.
Add -s/-es for he, she and it in positive sentences.
Form negatives and questions with do/does plus base verb.
Place common frequency words before a main verb.

explanation.en: Use present simple for usual habits: I get up at seven; she gets up at six. Add -s/-es for he/she/it in positive statements. For negatives and questions, use do or does plus the base verb: He doesn't walk; Does he walk? Frequency words such as always, often and usually normally go before the main action verb, but after be: She is often early. Do not use present continuous just because the sentence mentions today's timetable.
explanation.vi: Hiện tại đơn nói về thói quen. He/she/it thường thêm -s/-es. Phủ định và câu hỏi dùng do/does + động từ nguyên mẫu. Trạng từ tần suất thường đứng trước động từ thường nhưng đứng sau be.

examples: HABIT · I walk to school every weekday.
THIRD PERSON · My sister watches cartoons on Fridays.
NEGATIVE · He doesn't play chess. We don't play chess.
QUESTION · Does your dad cook? Yes, he does.
FREQUENCY · I usually read after dinner. She is often early.

activities.prompt: My sister ___ breakfast at seven every day.

feedback.explanation_en: An everyday routine with my sister takes the present simple eats.

activities.prompt: Complete: Tom ___ (watch) cartoons on Sundays.

feedback.explanation_en: Watch ends in -ch, so he/she/it takes watches.

activities.prompt: Which sentence is correct?

feedback.explanation_en: After doesn't, use base verb like, not likes.

activities.prompt: Complete: ___ (your friends / play) football after school?

feedback.explanation_en: Friends is plural; a present-simple question begins with do + subject + base verb.

activities.prompt: Which word best completes: 'I ___ do my homework before dinner.'

feedback.explanation_en: Usually describes how often a routine happens; the others point to different times.

activities.prompt: Choose the natural sentence.

feedback.explanation_en: With be, the frequency word normally follows is: She is often early.

activities.prompt: Complete: My parents ___ (not / work) on Saturdays.

feedback.explanation_en: Parents is plural; use don't/do not + base verb.

activities.prompt: Choose the correct short answer: Does Hoa read at night?

feedback.explanation_en: The auxiliary in the question is does, so the short answer is Yes, she does.

activities.prompt: Complete: My brother ___ (go) to music class on Fridays.

feedback.explanation_en: Go takes -es after he/she/it: goes.

activities.prompt: Which is a routine rather than an action happening now?

options.text: She visits her grandma every Saturday.

feedback.explanation_en: Every Saturday signals a repeated habit; the other statements describe current actions.

lessons.title: School places and classroom language
objectives: Recognise familiar school places and materials.
Use common classroom requests politely.
Understand words from short school notices.
Use place words in simple contexts.

explanation.en: Learn words in useful phrases, not as isolated translations: borrow a book from the library, practise in the gym, work in the science lab. Classroom requests include 'Could you repeat that, please?' and 'May I borrow a ruler?' Notice the place, person and action in each short sentence.
explanation.vi: Học từ theo cụm: borrow a book from the library; practise in the gym. Khi chưa hiểu, hỏi lịch sự: Could you repeat that, please?

examples: LIBRARY · You can borrow a book from the library.
GYM · We practise basketball in the gym.
LAB · Wear safety glasses in the science lab.
ASK · Could you repeat that, please?
BORROW · May I borrow your ruler?

activities.prompt: Where do students usually borrow books?

feedback.explanation_en: Borrow books is associated with a library.

activities.prompt: A teacher speaks too quickly. Which request is polite?

feedback.explanation_en: Could you repeat that, please? is a polite request for repetition.

activities.prompt: Complete: We eat lunch in the school ___.

feedback.explanation_en: A canteen or cafeteria is a place where students eat at school.

activities.prompt: Which item helps you draw a straight line?

feedback.explanation_en: A ruler helps you draw or measure straight lines.

activities.prompt: Which activity belongs in a science lab?

feedback.explanation_en: A laboratory is a place for practical scientific work.

activities.prompt: Complete: May I ___ your pencil for a minute?

feedback.explanation_en: Borrow means use something temporarily and return it later.

activities.prompt: A notice says 'Keep the corridor clear'. What should you do?

options.text: Make space for people to walk

feedback.explanation_en: A corridor is a hallway; keeping it clear lets people walk safely.

activities.prompt: Choose the natural phrase.

feedback.explanation_en: English uses do homework.

lessons.title: Daily activities and frequency
objectives: Name common actions in a school-day routine.
Recognise and use go, have, do and make in common phrases.
Distinguish frequency words in context.
Describe a routine in meaningful chunks.

explanation.en: Words become easier to remember in natural chunks: get up, have breakfast, catch the bus, do homework, go to bed. Often means many times; sometimes means on some occasions; never means not at any time. To describe your own day, use two or three phrases in a meaningful order.
explanation.vi: Học từ theo cụm tự nhiên: get up, have breakfast, catch the bus, do homework, go to bed. Often = thường xuyên; sometimes = thỉnh thoảng; never = không bao giờ.

examples: MORNING · I get up, have breakfast and catch the bus.
AFTER SCHOOL · I do homework and meet my friends.
EVENING · We have dinner before I go to bed.
FREQUENCY · I often read. I sometimes draw. I never skip breakfast.
USEFUL CHUNK · Make a plan, but do homework.

activities.prompt: Which phrase means wake and leave your bed?

feedback.explanation_en: Get up means rise from bed.

activities.prompt: Complete: I usually ___ breakfast before school.

feedback.explanation_en: Have breakfast and eat breakfast are both natural.

activities.prompt: Choose the natural phrase.

feedback.explanation_en: Do homework is the usual collocation.

activities.prompt: If you never walk to school, you walk there ___.

feedback.explanation_en: Never means not at any time.

activities.prompt: Complete: I ___ the bus at half past seven.

feedback.explanation_en: Catch/take the bus means use a bus for travel.

activities.prompt: Which activity is part of an evening bedtime routine rather than a morning routine?

options.text: having breakfast at the start of the day
brushing your teeth before going to sleep
arriving at school in the morning

feedback.explanation_en: Brushing your teeth before going to sleep is an evening bedtime activity. Breakfast, arriving at school and catching the morning bus belong to a morning routine.

activities.prompt: Choose the natural phrase for preparing what to do.

feedback.explanation_en: Make a plan is a standard collocation.

activities.prompt: Complete: I ___ go to the sports club on Fridays, but not every week.

feedback.explanation_en: Sometimes fits an activity that happens on some Fridays, not every week.

lessons.title: A new art club at school
objectives: Find the topic and purpose of a simple school notice.
Locate time, place and materials in the text.
Distinguish what students must bring from what the club provides.
Use a line of text to support an answer.

explanation.en: Read the whole notice once to understand its purpose. Then underline the exact phrase needed for each question: when, where, what to bring and how to join. A wrong answer may repeat a word from the passage but change its meaning. Go back to the sentence before choosing.
explanation.vi: Đọc một lượt để hiểu thông báo nói về việc gì. Khi trả lời, tìm đúng câu chứa bằng chứng: thời gian, địa điểm, đồ cần mang hoặc cách đăng ký.

examples: GIST · What is this notice mainly about? An art club.
DETAIL · 'three thirty' is the starting time; 'four thirty' is the finishing time.
CONTRAST · The club provides paint; students bring a pencil and notebook.
EVIDENCE · Underline the sentence that proves your answer, not just a familiar word.

activities.prompt: What is the main purpose of the notice?

options.text: To invite students to an art club

feedback.explanation_en: The notice explains what the new club does and how students can join.

activities.prompt: Where does the club meet?

feedback.explanation_en: The second sentence identifies Room 12.

activities.prompt: On which day does the club meet?

feedback.explanation_en: The club meets on Wednesdays after class.

activities.prompt: What time does the club finish?

feedback.explanation_en: The notice says it finishes at four thirty, or 16:30.

activities.prompt: What should a new student bring?

feedback.explanation_en: Paint is provided; a personal pencil and notebook are requested.

activities.prompt: What did students make last week?

feedback.explanation_en: Last week's work was colourful garden signs; this week's poster has a different topic.

activities.prompt: Can someone join if they missed the first week?

options.text: Yes, new students may join at any time.
No, only the first eight students may join.
Only at the end of the year.

feedback.explanation_en: The notice explicitly welcomes new students at any time.

activities.prompt: How can students register?

options.text: Write their name outside the library before Wednesday lunch
Send a letter to the gym

feedback.explanation_en: The last sentence gives the registration location and deadline.

reading_asset.title: Art club notice
reading_asset.body: Our school has a new art club. It meets in Room 12 on Wednesdays after class. The club starts at three thirty and finishes at four thirty. Ms Hoa helps students draw, paint and make posters. You do not need to bring paint because the club has art materials. Bring your own pencil and a small notebook. Last week, eight students joined. They made colourful signs for the school garden. This week, the group will design a poster about saving water. New students can join at any time. To register, write your name on the list outside the library before Wednesday lunch.

lessons.title: A class book exchange
objectives: Find the purpose and details of a short event announcement.
Understand the condition attached to tickets.
Distinguish facts explicitly stated from reasonable inference.
Explain a contrast signalled by however.

explanation.en: Before answering, identify the event's purpose and sequence. For detail questions, locate the line with a time, rule or person. For inference, connect two statements without adding facts that are not in the text. However signals a change from an earlier idea to the final decision.
explanation.vi: Đọc để tìm mục đích, quy định và trình tự sự kiện. 'However' báo hiệu sự thay đổi ý. Suy luận cần dựa vào câu chữ trong bài, không tự thêm thông tin.

examples: GIST · This is an announcement about sharing used books.
RULE · Tickets exchange for books, not food or stationery.
CONTRAST · They considered selling, but chose exchange so no payment was needed.
INFERENCE · You can attend without bringing a book, though you receive no book ticket.
EVIDENCE · Match every answer to a sentence or linked pair of sentences.

activities.prompt: Why did the team choose an exchange instead of selling books?

options.text: They wanted the event to be free to share stories.

feedback.explanation_en: However introduces the final decision: sharing without spending money.

activities.prompt: What condition must the books students bring to exchange meet?

options.text: They must be in good condition.
They must be bought this month.

feedback.explanation_en: The notice says students can bring books they have finished reading as long as those books are in good condition.

activities.prompt: When will the event begin?

feedback.explanation_en: The meeting time is Friday at three; half past four concerns remaining books.

activities.prompt: What can a student do with one ticket?

feedback.explanation_en: Tickets can be exchanged for different books, not food or stationery.

activities.prompt: What can a student without a book do?

options.text: Attend and read in the quiet corner
Take any book home without a ticket

feedback.explanation_en: The announcement welcomes students without books to visit and read.

activities.prompt: What happens to books left at 4:30?

options.text: They are offered to the school library.

feedback.explanation_en: The leftover books are offered to the library; the librarian then decides suitability.

activities.prompt: Who will organise the activities?

feedback.explanation_en: Parents may help with tables, but students organise activities themselves.

activities.prompt: Why is the word 'However' used?

options.text: To show a contrast between selling and exchanging
To give the exact starting time

feedback.explanation_en: However marks the difference between the considered option and the chosen plan.

reading_asset.title: Book exchange announcement
reading_asset.body: Our class is planning a small book exchange next Friday. Students may bring one or two books they have finished reading, as long as the books are in good condition. We will meet in the school hall at three o'clock. First, volunteers will put the books on tables by topic. Each student will receive a ticket for every book they bring. A ticket can be exchanged for a different book, but it cannot be used to buy food or stationery. Students who cannot bring a book can still visit the event and read in the quiet corner. The organising team considered selling the books to raise money. However, they chose an exchange because they wanted everyone to share stories without spending money. At half past four, any books left on the tables will be offered to the school library. The librarian will choose which titles are suitable for the collection. Parents are welcome to help with the tables, but students will organise the activities themselves. Please write your name on the volunteer list by Wednesday if you can help.

lessons.title: Introduce yourself in a short paragraph
objectives: Identify what a short self-introduction must include.
Choose relevant details and put them in a clear order.
Write short connected sentences using familiar vocabulary.
Review your draft and improve one sentence after feedback.

explanation.en: Read the task and underline the person you are writing to, the information requested and the word range. Brainstorm two details about yourself, choose the useful ones, and make a simple order: greeting, name/age, school or hobby, friendly ending. Write your own sentences. Before submitting, check the subject and verb, capital I, full stops and whether each requested detail is present. You can revise after an adult reviews the actual text. Word count is guidance, not a quality score.
explanation.vi: Phân tích đề: viết cho ai, phải nói những gì. Nghĩ nhanh vài ý, chọn ý phù hợp, xếp theo thứ tự mở đầu → thông tin bản thân → sở thích → kết thúc. Tự kiểm tra I viết hoa, chủ ngữ/động từ và dấu chấm. Độ dài không phải điểm năng lực.

examples: ANALYSE · Audience: a new classmate. Include your name, one school detail and a hobby.
BRAINSTORM · Name: Linh; favourite subject: science; hobby: drawing.
PLAN · Greeting → name → school detail → hobby → friendly ending.
MODEL · Hi, I'm Linh. I am in class six. I like science because I enjoy experiments. In my free time, I draw pictures. What do you enjoy doing?
SELF-CHECK · Does every sentence answer the task? Check I/am, capitals, punctuation and spelling.

activities.prompt: A new classmate asks you to introduce yourself. What should you include?

options.text: Only a list of your favourite foods
Your name and a few relevant facts about yourself
An address for every family member

feedback.explanation_en: The task asks for a short, relevant introduction, not unrelated or private details.

activities.prompt: Which order is clearest for a short introduction?

options.text: Greeting → name → school detail → hobby → friendly ending

feedback.explanation_en: An introduction is easier to follow when it starts with greeting/name and ends naturally.

activities.prompt: Choose a complete and correct sentence.

feedback.explanation_en: Use I am and a complete sentence.

activities.prompt: Which detail develops 'I like drawing'?

options.text: I draw animals in my notebook after school.

feedback.explanation_en: A specific example supports the hobby rather than repeating or changing topic.

activities.prompt: Write a friendly self-introduction to a new classmate. Include your name or nickname, one school detail and one hobby. Aim for about 35–55 words. First plan your ideas, then write your own paragraph. Do not include an address, phone number or other private information.

lessons.title: Present simple or present continuous?
objectives: Decide whether a sentence describes a routine, an action happening now or a temporary arrangement.
Use present simple and present continuous in positive, negative and question forms.
Choose correct verb agreement and distinguish common state verbs.
Enter only the missing word or phrase when completing a sentence.

explanation.en: Meaning first: the present simple describes routines and general facts; the present continuous (am/is/are + verb-ing) describes an action happening now or a temporary situation. Compare 'I usually walk to school' with 'I am taking the bus today'. For the simple, add -s/-es with he, she and it; in negatives and questions use does/doesn't + the base verb, not 'doesn't plays'. For the continuous, remember the correct form of be, including in questions: 'Are they playing?' Some state verbs, such as know, usually take the simple here. Time phrases help, but decide from the meaning. For a gap-fill, type only what belongs in the gap.
explanation.vi: Hiểu ý nghĩa trước: hiện tại đơn diễn tả thói quen hoặc sự thật chung; hiện tại tiếp diễn (am/is/are + V-ing) diễn tả việc đang xảy ra hoặc tình huống tạm thời. Với he/she/it, thêm -s/-es ở câu khẳng định; sau does/doesn't dùng động từ nguyên mẫu. Câu tiếp diễn phải có am/is/are. Các từ chỉ thời gian chỉ là gợi ý, không thay thế việc hiểu ngữ cảnh. Nếu đề có chỗ trống, chỉ điền phần còn thiếu, không lặp lại chủ ngữ.

examples: ROUTINE · Maya walks to school most days. The present simple describes her usual habit.
NOW · Look! Maya is walking to the gate. The present continuous describes what is happening.
TEMPORARY · This week, Maya is staying with her aunt. This is not necessarily her usual home.
SIMPLE FORMS · He plays. He doesn't play. Does he play? After does/doesn't, use play, not plays.
CONTINUOUS FORMS · They are playing. They aren't playing. Are they playing? Include the correct form of be.
STATE VERB · She knows the answer. In this meaning, 'is knowing' is not natural.
ANSWER FORMAT · My brother usually ___ (study) → studies. Don't repeat 'My brother' in the answer.
SELF-CHECK · Ask: Is it a routine, happening now or temporary? Does the subject agree with the verb?

activities.prompt: Every Saturday, Maya ___ at the community garden.

feedback.explanation_en: 'Every Saturday' indicates the normal routine. Maya is one person, so use volunteers. 'Volunteer' lacks third-person -s; 'is volunteering' would suggest a current or temporary activity rather than the habitual meaning here.

activities.prompt: Be quiet! The children ___ a story.

feedback.explanation_en: 'Be quiet!' points to an action happening now. 'Children' is plural, so the correct form is are reading, not is reading. The present simple would describe a routine rather than this current action.

activities.prompt: Complete: My brother usually ___ (study) after dinner.

feedback.explanation_en: 'Usually' describes a habit. 'My brother' is third-person singular: study changes to studies (consonant + y → ies). Enter just studies, not a full sentence.

activities.prompt: Which sentence expresses a temporary situation?

options.text: I am staying with my aunt this week.
Water boils at 100°C at sea level.

feedback.explanation_en: 'This week' describes a temporary arrangement, so 'I am staying with my aunt this week' fits. The other choices describe a usual situation, a general fact or a repeated hobby.

activities.prompt: Complete: Look! It ___ (rain).

feedback.explanation_en: 'Look!' describes what is happening now. It + is + raining makes 'Look! It is raining.' Type only is raining: 'it's raining' would repeat the subject already printed in the question.

activities.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.

feedback.explanation_en: Know describes a state in this meaning, so use the present simple: She knows the answer. 'Know' needs -s with she; 'is knowing' is not the natural form here.

activities.prompt: Leo usually ___ to school, but today he ___ the bus because of the rain.

feedback.explanation_en: 'Usually' describes Leo's routine, so use walks with third-person -s. 'But today' contrasts the temporary situation, so use is taking. The two clauses need different tenses.

activities.prompt: Complete: Why ___ (you / wear) a coat today?

feedback.explanation_en: This asks about an action or temporary situation today. After 'Why', the continuous question order is are + you + wearing. Enter only are you wearing, not another Why.

activities.prompt: Which sentence correctly describes a routine?

options.text: She doesn't plays tennis on Mondays.
She don't play tennis on Mondays.
She doesn't play tennis on Mondays.
She isn't play tennis on Mondays.

feedback.explanation_en: For a repeated routine, use the present simple. With 'she', the negative is doesn't + base verb: doesn't play. Do not add -s after doesn't; 'don't' disagrees with she.

activities.prompt: Complete: My parents ___ (not / work) on Sundays.

reading_asset.title: What makes practice effective?
reading_asset.body: People sometimes assume that learning a new skill requires long, uninterrupted periods of study. In practice, shorter sessions can be useful when they are regular and purposeful. A learner who practises for fifteen minutes every day may remember more than someone who works for two hours once a week, especially if the shorter sessions include a quick review of earlier material. This does not mean long sessions are always ineffective. They can be valuable for complex projects that demand sustained attention. The important question is not simply how long a session lasts, but what the learner does during it. For example, rereading notes can feel productive without revealing what has been forgotten. Trying to explain an idea from memory, checking the explanation and correcting errors gives clearer evidence of understanding. Rest also matters. When learners notice that attention is falling, a short break may be more useful than forcing themselves to continue. A sustainable study plan therefore combines focused practice, regular review and time to recover.

objectives: Use in, on and under to describe simple positions.

explanation.en: A preposition of place tells where one thing is relative to another. In means inside; on means on a surface; under means below; next to means beside. Between normally places a thing in the space separating two named things. In front of points to the nearer/front side; behind is on the back side. lessons.title: A class visit to the science museum
objectives: Understand the main purpose of a simple trip notice.
Find departure, meeting and return times without mixing them up.

TIME · Meet at 8:30; the bus departs at 8:45.

lessons.title: A garden project changes its plan
objectives: Identify the main purpose of a school project update.
Follow revised plans and conditional activities.
Distinguish supplied materials from optional contributions.
Use contrast and condition language as evidence.

explanation.en: Read the update as a changed plan rather than a list of unrelated events. Mark the original plan, the reason for changing it and the new timetable. 'However' signals a contrast; 'only if' means an activity depends on a condition. Do not treat an optional contribution as a requirement.
explanation.vi: Đây là thông báo thay đổi kế hoạch. Tìm kế hoạch ban đầu, lý do đổi và lịch mới. 'However' báo hiệu sự tương phản; 'only if' là điều kiện bắt buộc để hoạt động xảy ra.

Nobody may use tools on Sunday.

options.text: Spare flowerpots are welcome, but buying supplies is unnecessary.
Families should arrive before nine on Friday.

feedback.explanation_en: Flowerpots are optional; the text says buying new supplies is not necessary.

reading_asset.title: Student council garden update
reading_asset.body: The student council is organising a weekend project to improve the small garden behind the school. The original plan was to plant flowers and paint the benches on the same day. lessons.title: Write a friendly invitation message
objectives: Identify the recipient and the details requested in a short invitation.
Choose a day, time, place and activity relevant to the prompt.
Organise a greeting, invitation and friendly ending.
Check that each requested detail is present before sending.

explanation.en: Analyse the task before writing: Who is your reader? What event are you inviting them to? Which details must be included? Brainstorm two possible activities, choose one, then plan: greeting → invitation → day and time → meeting place → friendly ending. Write short complete sentences. Check the day, time and place, basic verb forms, capital letters and punctuation. Adult feedback should lead to a revision you write yourself.
explanation.vi: Phân tích đề: mời ai, làm gì, khi nào, gặp ở đâu. Nghĩ vài ý, chọn một ý phù hợp, lập dàn ý lời chào → lời mời → ngày/giờ/địa điểm → kết thúc. Tự kiểm tra đủ thông tin rồi mới nộp.

examples: TASK · Invite a classmate to an art club event. Include a day, time and meeting place.
BRAINSTORM · Draw a poster or paint a picture; choose the activity you can explain clearly.
PLAN · Hi Anna → Would you like to...? → On Saturday at 10 → Meet outside the library → See you!
MODEL · Hi Anna! Would you like to join the art club with me on Saturday? It starts at ten. Let's meet outside the library at quarter to ten. We can draw a poster together. See you!
SELF-CHECK · Can your friend tell when, where and what to do? Is the tone friendly?

activities.prompt: Your classmate asks you to invite them to an art event. What details are needed?

options.text: The event, when it happens and where to meet

feedback.explanation_en: An actionable invitation includes the event, time and meeting place.

activities.prompt: Which opening is appropriate for a friendly message?

options.text: Dear Sir or Madam, I hereby request...
Hi Mia! Would you like to join me?

feedback.explanation_en: A friendly greeting and invitation fit a message to a classmate.

options.text: Greeting → invitation → day/time → meeting place → ending

feedback.explanation_en: The recipient first learns what they are invited to, then when and where.

options.text: Let's meet outside the school library.

feedback.explanation_en: Outside the school library identifies where to meet clearly.

lessons.title: Describe a school event in an email
objectives: Identify the audience and three content requirements of an email task.
Select relevant details and expand one activity with a reason or example.
Write a clear beginning, middle and ending.
Revise based on feedback without copying a model verbatim.

explanation.en: Read the prompt and underline the reader, purpose and each requested detail. Brainstorm possible school events, choose one real or imaginary event, then select only details that answer the task. Plan: greeting → where/when → what happened → what you liked and why → friendly ending. Use past simple for finished events, but check each verb individually. After drafting, compare your text to the task and revise one weak sentence independently.
explanation.vi: Phân tích đề: người đọc, mục đích và ba yêu cầu nội dung. Brainstorm một vài sự kiện, chọn một, chọn chi tiết liên quan. Dàn ý: chào → khi nào/ở đâu → đã làm gì → thích gì và vì sao → kết thư. Sửa dựa trên phản hồi, không chép lại bài mẫu.

examples: TASK · Email a friend about an event: when/where, one activity, what you enjoyed and why.
BRAINSTORM · Science fair: Friday afternoon; saw a robot; enjoyed building a model.
SELECT · Keep details that answer the three required points; remove unrelated shopping plans.
PLAN · Hi Sam → event time/place → main activity → favourite part + reason → write back soon.

MODEL · Hi Sam! Last Friday our school held a science fair in the hall. My class built a simple robot. I liked testing it because we solved a problem together. It was noisy but exciting. Have you visited a school fair? Write soon, Linh.
SELF-CHECK · Have you answered every part? Are past events expressed clearly? Does your ending fit a friend?

activities.prompt: Your friend asks about a school event. Which detail belongs in the reply?

feedback.explanation_en: The task asks for information about the event, beginning with when and where.

I liked it. I liked it. I liked it.
It was in April, but I will not explain.

Only list the event name five times

We building a model last Friday.

lessons.title: Can, can't and basic requests
objectives: Express simple present ability using can and can't.
Ask about ability and give short answers.
Make a polite basic request with Can you ... please?
Use the base form of a verb after can or can't.

explanation.en: Can expresses an ability now: I can ride a bike. Can't or cannot expresses lack of ability: She can't swim yet. Can does not change after he, she or it, and the next verb stays in its base form: He can draw, not 'cans draws'. Questions put can before the subject: Can you swim? Yes, I can. No, I can't. A polite everyday request can use Can you open the window, please? Read whether the sentence asks about ability or requests help. For gap tasks, type only the missing word or phrase.
explanation.vi: Can diễn tả khả năng hiện tại, can't/cannot là chưa thể làm được. Sau can/can't dùng động từ nguyên mẫu, không thêm -s hoặc to. Đảo can lên trước chủ ngữ để hỏi. Lời nhờ lịch sự: Can you ... please? Chỉ điền phần thiếu.

examples: ABILITY · Nia can ride a bicycle now.
NO ABILITY · Ben can't swim yet; he is learning.
QUESTION · Can you draw a map? Yes, I can.
REQUEST · Can you pass me the notebook, please?
FORM · She can sing, not 'she cans sings'.
GAP · My brother ___ (not / swim) yet. → can't swim / cannot swim.

activities.prompt: Lina has learned to swim and can swim across the pool. Choose the sentence that reports her ability.

feedback.explanation_en: Can is followed by the base verb swim. Do not add -s after can, use swimming after can, or omit to from is able to swim.

activities.prompt: Use can/can't to describe present ability. Complete with the missing phrase only: My little brother has not learned to ride yet; he ___ (not / ride) a bicycle.

feedback.explanation_en: The task specifically asks for ability with can/can't. Use can't ride or cannot ride, followed by the base verb ride. 'Doesn't ride' is grammatical elsewhere, but it does not use the requested modal form.

activities.prompt: Which request to a classmate is the most polite?

Can you pass me the pencil?
You must pass me the pencil.

feedback.explanation_en: All the sentences ask for or demand the pencil, but Can you ... please? combines a question with please and is the most polite in this context. An imperative is more direct.

activities.prompt: Complete with can (write the missing word only): ___ you help me carry these books, please?

feedback.explanation_en: The instruction specifies can. Put Can before you to make a basic polite request. Could/would/will can be natural requests elsewhere, but this gap practises can specifically.

activities.prompt: Choose the correct short answer: Can your sister play chess? (She has not learned yet.)

feedback.explanation_en: Can questions take can/can't in the short answer; the context says she has not learned.

activities.prompt: Complete: She ___ (can / draw) animals very well.

feedback.explanation_en: Can is unchanged with she and is followed by the base verb draw.

activities.prompt: Choose the correct form after can.

feedback.explanation_en: Use can play, without third-person -s, -ing or cans.

activities.prompt: Complete: ___ he play chess? Yes, he can.

feedback.explanation_en: The ability question begins with Can. Do not repeat he, which is already printed.

activities.prompt: Which sentence correctly says that two children have the ability to read?

feedback.explanation_en: Can stays the same with plural subjects; read is the base verb.

activities.prompt: Use can/can't to describe present ability. Complete with the missing phrase only: I have never learned German; I ___ (not / speak) it yet.

feedback.explanation_en: This task specifically practises can/can't for ability: can't speak or cannot speak. In other contexts don't speak is grammatical, but it does not use the requested modal form.

lessons.title: Past simple forms, negatives and questions
objectives: Use regular and common irregular verbs for finished past events.
Form negatives with didn't + base verb.
Make questions with Did + subject + base verb.
Use was/were for past forms of be and distinguish them from did.

explanation.en: The past simple describes a completed event at a stated or understood past time: We visited the museum yesterday. Most regular verbs take -ed, while common irregular verbs change form: go → went, buy → bought. For an ordinary action-verb negative, use didn't/did not + the base verb: We didn't go, not 'didn't went'. Questions use Did + subject + base verb: Did you visit? Past be is different: I/he/she was; you/we/they were. Do not add did to 'was/were' questions. A past-time phrase helps, but check which action the sentence describes. Type only the missing phrase in a gap.
explanation.vi: Quá khứ đơn diễn tả việc đã kết thúc. Động từ thường thêm -ed hoặc có dạng bất quy tắc (go → went). Phủ định dùng didn't + V nguyên mẫu, câu hỏi Did + chủ ngữ + V nguyên mẫu. Be ở quá khứ dùng was/were, không thêm did trước was/were.

examples: FINISHED · We visited the museum yesterday.
IRREGULAR · She went home after the match.
NEGATIVE · I didn't watch the film last night.
QUESTION · Did you go to the art club?
BE · He was late; they were early.
GAP · They ___ (not / play) yesterday. → didn't play / did not play.

activities.prompt: Complete: We ___ the museum yesterday afternoon.

feedback.explanation_en: Yesterday afternoon gives a completed past time; visited is the regular past form of visit.

activities.prompt: Complete in the past simple; enter the missing phrase only: I ___ (not / watch) television last night.

feedback.explanation_en: Use didn't/did not + base verb watch for the past simple negative. Past continuous could fit a different situation, but the requested tense here is past simple.

activities.prompt: Which question asks about a finished event last Sunday?

options.text: Did you go to the market last Sunday?
Do you went to the market last Sunday?
Did you went to the market last Sunday?
Are you go to the market last Sunday?

feedback.explanation_en: Did + subject + base verb go forms a past-simple action question.

activities.prompt: Complete: Yesterday, Maya ___ (buy) a new notebook.

feedback.explanation_en: Buy is irregular: the past simple is bought, not buyed.

activities.prompt: Choose the correct negative sentence.

feedback.explanation_en: The past-simple negative of an action verb is didn't + base verb play.

activities.prompt: Complete: Where ___ you go last weekend?

feedback.explanation_en: The printed subject and base verb are already present: Where did you go ...?

activities.prompt: Complete: Last month, our class ___ on a school trip.

feedback.explanation_en: Go has the irregular past form went, used for a finished past trip.

activities.prompt: Complete: They ___ (be) at the library yesterday.

feedback.explanation_en: They takes were in the past simple of be. Do not add did.

activities.prompt: Choose the correct past-simple question using be.

feedback.explanation_en: Past be questions invert was and the subject: Was she ...? Do not use did.

activities.prompt: Use the past simple to complete the gap; enter the missing phrase only: She ___ (not / go) to the club last Tuesday.

feedback.explanation_en: The requested past-simple negative is didn't go or did not go. After did not, use the base verb go. Another tense needs different intended meaning.

lessons.title: Countability, some/any, much/many
objectives: Distinguish common countable and uncountable nouns in everyday contexts.
Use many with plural countable nouns and much with uncountable nouns.
Use some in ordinary affirmative statements and any in neutral questions/negatives.
Choose a quantity expression based on both noun type and sentence meaning.

explanation.en: Countable nouns have singular and plural forms: one apple, three apples; ask how many apples. Uncountable nouns such as rice, water and milk do not normally take -s in these meanings; ask how much rice. Use some in ordinary affirmative statements: We have some bread. Any is common in neutral information questions and negatives: Are there any chairs? There aren't any chairs. Some can also appear in offers and requests when you expect a positive response, so always read the context rather than memorising an absolute rule. Use much with uncountable nouns and many with plural countable nouns. A unit phrase can make an uncountable substance countable: two bottles of water.
explanation.vi: Danh từ đếm được có dạng số ít/số nhiều; danh từ không đếm được như rice, water, milk thường không thêm -s theo nghĩa này. How many + số nhiều đếm được; how much + không đếm được. Some thường ở câu khẳng định, any thường ở câu hỏi trung tính/phủ định; vẫn có ngoại lệ theo mục đích nói.

examples: COUNTABLE · three apples; How many apples?
UNCOUNTABLE · some rice; How much rice?
AFFIRMATIVE · There are some books on the shelf.
NEGATIVE · There aren't any eggs in the box.
QUESTION · Are there any chairs in the hall?
UNIT · two bottles of water, not 'two waters' for two bottles.

activities.prompt: Which noun is usually uncountable when it means food in general?

feedback.explanation_en: Rice names a substance in this meaning; the other options are countable items.

activities.prompt: Complete: How ___ chairs are there in the hall?

feedback.explanation_en: Chairs is a plural countable noun, so use how many.

activities.prompt: Complete: How ___ water do we need for the trip?

feedback.explanation_en: Water is uncountable in this context, so the quantity question uses how much.

activities.prompt: Choose from some or any; type one word. The fridge is empty: there are zero eggs. There aren't ___ eggs in the fridge.

feedback.explanation_en: Use any (not some) in this negative statement to express that there are zero eggs. Many/enough would express a different quantity judgement, but the given choice is some or any.

activities.prompt: Which sentence uses some naturally in an ordinary affirmative statement?

options.text: I have some apples in my bag.
I have any apples in my bag.
I have much apples in my bag.
I have an apples in my bag.

feedback.explanation_en: Some apples is natural in a simple affirmative statement with plural countable apples.

activities.prompt: Choose from some or any; type one word. We need ___ oranges for the picnic; please add them to the shopping list.

feedback.explanation_en: Some fits this ordinary affirmative statement. The task limits the choice to some or any; other quantity words may work in different sentences, but they are not being tested here.

activities.prompt: A recipe needs milk as a liquid ingredient, not a café serving. Which noun phrase naturally refers to an unspecified amount?

feedback.explanation_en: Some milk treats milk as an uncountable ingredient in the recipe. A milk and three milks can name servings in a café, but not the intended uncountable quantity here.

activities.prompt: Complete: How ___ milk is left in the bottle?

feedback.explanation_en: Milk is an uncountable liquid in this sentence; use how much.

activities.prompt: Which expression clearly counts containers rather than the water itself?

feedback.explanation_en: Bottles is countable, so two bottles of water names two containers of an uncountable substance.

activities.prompt: Choose from some or any; type one word. I have ___ rice at home and will use it for dinner.

feedback.explanation_en: Some fits an ordinary affirmative statement about rice. It describes an unspecified quantity, not proof that the amount is enough; this task contrasts some with any.

lessons.title: Comparatives and superlatives
objectives: Use comparative forms with than for two people or things.
Use the + superlative for one item in a defined group of three or more.
Form common -er/-est and more/most patterns.
Use irregular better/best and worse/worst accurately.

explanation.en: To compare two things, often use an adjective's comparative form plus than: taller than; more interesting than. Many short adjectives use -er, and consonant + y changes to -ier: heavy → heavier. Longer adjectives often use more or most. A superlative identifies an extreme within a defined group: the tallest of three. The is generally used before the superlative in these examples. Common irregular forms include good → better → best and bad → worse → worst. Do not say 'more taller' or 'the most fastest'. For gap answers, enter only what replaces the blank.
explanation.vi: So sánh hơn giữa hai đối tượng thường dùng -er/more ... than. So sánh nhất trong một nhóm thường dùng the -est/the most ... . Heavy → heavier/heaviest; good → better/best; bad → worse/worst. Tránh dùng đồng thời more + -er hoặc most + -est.

examples: TWO · This pencil is longer than that one.
LONG ADJECTIVE · This story is more interesting than the first.
THREE · Of the three bags, the blue bag is the lightest.
SPELLING · heavy → heavier → heaviest.
IRREGULAR · good → better → best.
CONTRAST · taller than, not 'more taller than'.

activities.prompt: Complete: Mai is ___ than her brother.

feedback.explanation_en: Than compares two people, so the comparative form taller is needed.

activities.prompt: Complete: This schoolbag is ___ (heavy) than that one.

feedback.explanation_en: Heavy ends in consonant + y; change y to i and add -er for heavier.

activities.prompt: Which sentence selects one book as the most interesting of three?

options.text: This is the most interesting of the three books.
This is more interesting of the three books.
This is the more interesting of the three books.
This is the most interesting than the other two books.

feedback.explanation_en: A group of three calls for the superlative the most interesting of the three. The comparative more interesting needs than and a specific comparison; a superlative is not followed by than here.

activities.prompt: Complete: Of the three buses, the red one is the ___ (fast).

feedback.explanation_en: The fastest is the superlative within a group of three buses; the is already printed.

activities.prompt: Complete: This answer is ___ than my first answer.

feedback.explanation_en: Good has the irregular comparative better; do not combine more and better.

activities.prompt: Complete: Of all four posters, I think this is the ___ (good).

feedback.explanation_en: Good changes to best for a superlative in the defined group of four posters.

activities.prompt: Which phrase correctly compares how exciting two events are?

feedback.explanation_en: Use more exciting than to compare the quality of two events. Most exciting is a superlative, while excited generally describes a person's feeling, not the event's quality.

activities.prompt: Complete: This book is ___ (interesting) than the first one.

feedback.explanation_en: Interesting commonly takes more for comparison of two books, not -er.

activities.prompt: Which sentence uses a superlative naturally?

options.text: My bag is the lightest of the three.
My bag is lighter of the three.
My bag is the more lightest of the three.
My bag is most lighter of the three.

feedback.explanation_en: The lightest correctly selects the extreme in a group of three.

activities.prompt: Complete: Today the weather is ___ (bad) than yesterday.

feedback.explanation_en: Bad has irregular comparative worse; than shows a comparison between two days.

lessons.title: Travel and event collocations in context
objectives: Recognise frequent travel and event word partnerships in context.
Distinguish book a ticket, catch/miss a bus and pack a bag.
Use take photos and attend an event naturally.
Select a collocation from the meaning of the whole situation.

explanation.en: A collocation is a word partnership often used together. We book a ticket to reserve a seat, pack a bag before leaving, catch a bus when we get on in time, and miss a bus if it leaves before we arrive. We arrive at a station but arrive in a city. At an event, we may attend a workshop and take photos. Read the time and purpose in each sentence, not just the nearest noun. Other phrases may be grammatical in different situations, so select the expression that fits the stated meaning.
explanation.vi: Collocation là các từ thường đi với nhau. Book a ticket = đặt vé; pack a bag = xếp đồ; catch/miss a bus = bắt/lỡ xe. Arrive at a station nhưng arrive in a city. Attend a workshop và take photos. Xét cả ngữ cảnh trước khi chọn.

examples: BOOK · We booked two train tickets on Tuesday.
PACK · I packed my bag before the school trip.
CATCH · We left early to catch the eight o'clock bus.
MISS · The bus left without us; we missed it.
ARRIVE · Arrive at the station; arrive in the city.
EVENT · Attend a workshop and take photos afterward.

activities.prompt: You want to reserve a train seat in advance, not check, cancel or simply pay for a ticket at the counter. Which phrase means make a reservation?

feedback.explanation_en: Book a ticket means reserve it in advance. Buy refers to paying, check to inspecting and cancel to ending the reservation; booking may also involve payment, but the question asks specifically about reserving.

activities.prompt: Choose from pack or book; type one word. Before a trip, please ___ your bag tonight by putting your clothes and notebook inside.

feedback.explanation_en: Pack a bag means put the items needed for a trip inside it. The task limits the choice to pack or book; book is used for reserving tickets or accommodation, not filling a bag.

activities.prompt: You planned to take the eight o'clock bus, but it had already left when you reached the stop. Which sentence best describes what happened to that bus?

options.text: You caught the eight o'clock bus.
You missed the eight o'clock bus.
You waited at the stop for the eight o'clock bus before it left.
You arrived early and got on the eight o'clock bus.

feedback.explanation_en: You missed the eight o'clock bus because it departed before you arrived. The other choices would require arriving in time to catch or wait for that bus.

activities.prompt: Which phrase gives the natural arrival expression for a station?

feedback.explanation_en: Arrive at is the normal expression for a specific point such as a station.

activities.prompt: At the science fair, you pointed a camera at an exhibit and pressed the shutter. Which action did you perform?

feedback.explanation_en: Take photos means use the camera to create pictures. Looking, sharing and printing involve photos already taken; pressing the shutter is the taking action.

activities.prompt: You go to a weekend workshop as a student participant, not an organiser. Which action describes your role?

feedback.explanation_en: Attend a workshop means be present as a participant. Organise means plan it, cancel means call it off, and miss means not attend it.

activities.prompt: Complete: We will ___ the bus if we do not leave now; it is already at the stop.

feedback.explanation_en: The bus may leave without us, so the natural phrase is miss the bus.

activities.prompt: The organiser calls off the trip because the road is closed. The trip will not take place, and no later date is planned. Which action fits?

feedback.explanation_en: Cancel the trip means it will not take place. Postpone moves it to a later time; here no replacement date is planned.

lessons.title: A message about an art-club visit
objectives: Identify the sender's purpose in a short personal message.
Find an explicit meeting time and location.
Distinguish items the reader must bring from items supplied by the club.
Follow a simple changed plan and reply deadline.

explanation.en: Read the personal message and ask: Who is writing, why, where and when? Locate exact phrases for times and meeting places rather than guessing from the main event's starting time. Underline what the student must bring and what the club provides. Notice 'but' for a changed transport plan, 'if' for a condition and 'by Thursday' for the latest reply time. All answers should be supported by the message.
explanation.vi: Đọc tin nhắn, xác định ai viết, mục đích, giờ hẹn và địa điểm. Giờ gặp có thể khác giờ hoạt động bắt đầu. Phân biệt đồ phải mang theo và đồ được cung cấp. But thể hiện thay đổi, if là điều kiện, by Thursday là hạn chót.

examples: PURPOSE · The message makes plans for an art-club activity.
TIME · The club starts at 10 a.m.; the friends meet earlier at 9:30.
PLACE · The meeting point is outside the school library.
BRING/PROVIDE · Bring a pencil and sketchbook; the club provides paints.
CONDITION · Eat in the park if dry, but in the hall if it rains.
DEADLINE · Reply by Thursday.

activities.prompt: Why does Lan write to Minh?

options.text: To arrange their visit to an art-club activity
To arrange lunch only, not the club visit
To ask Minh to buy paints for the club
To announce that the library meeting place has changed to the park

feedback.explanation_en: Lan's main purpose is to arrange an art-club visit and receive Minh's reply. Lunch and supplies are supporting details; the message says the club provides paints and the meeting place is still the library.

activities.prompt: Where should Minh meet Lan?

feedback.explanation_en: The message explicitly gives outside the school library as their meeting point.

activities.prompt: When should the two friends meet?

feedback.explanation_en: The meeting is at 9:30 a.m., before the club starts at 10 a.m.

activities.prompt: What alternative to taking the bus does Lan mention?

options.text: Her father can give them a lift
A bus supplied by the art club

feedback.explanation_en: Lan says her father can give them a lift. Can describes an available alternative; the message does not confirm a final travel decision or state a vehicle type.

activities.prompt: Which items should Minh bring?

feedback.explanation_en: The message asks Minh to bring a pencil and his sketchbook.

activities.prompt: Does Minh need to bring paints?

options.text: Yes, he must buy new paints.
No, the club will provide them.
Yes, because the club has no paints.
No, because nobody will paint or draw.

feedback.explanation_en: The message states the club provides the paints, so bringing them is unnecessary.

activities.prompt: What will happen if it rains after the activity?

options.text: They will eat in the hall.
They will eat in the park anyway.
The friends must return to school immediately.
The event starts two hours earlier.

feedback.explanation_en: The conditional plan says they will eat in the hall if it rains.

activities.prompt: What is the latest day Lan asks Minh to reply?

feedback.explanation_en: The message says reply by Thursday so Lan can confirm numbers with the leader.

reading_asset.title: Lan's art-club message
reading_asset.body:
Hi Minh,
Our art club is meeting at the community hall on Saturday at 10 a.m. I planned to take the bus with you, but my father can give us a lift. Please meet me outside the school library at 9:30 a.m. Bring a pencil and your sketchbook. You don't need to bring paints because the club will provide them. We will design postcards for a local exhibition. After the activity, we can have lunch in the park if it is dry. If it rains, we will eat in the hall instead. I must leave by 2 p.m. to visit my grandmother. Could you reply by Thursday so I can tell the club leader how many people are coming?
See you,
Lan

lessons.title: Describe a familiar person or place
objectives: Identify the reader and required points in a short description.
Select relevant facts about one familiar person or place.
Connect simple sentences in a clear order.
Check the description independently before adult review.

explanation.en: First read the prompt and choose ONE subject: a familiar person at school or a familiar place at school. For a person, plan who they are, what they do and why you appreciate them. For a place, plan where it is, what you can see there and why you like it. Brainstorm short facts; select details that answer the chosen task. Write a clear opening and three or four connected sentences; then check capital letters, be, there is/are, simple present forms and punctuation. Use a made-up name if needed and do not include private contact details. Your own paragraph, not your word count, is the evidence for adult review.
explanation.vi: Đọc đề và chọn MỘT đối tượng: người quen ở trường hoặc địa điểm trong trường. Với người: họ là ai, làm gì, vì sao em quý họ. Với nơi chốn: ở đâu, có gì, vì sao em thích. Brainstorm, chọn chi tiết liên quan, viết câu mở đầu và vài câu nối tiếp, rồi tự kiểm tra. Không đưa thông tin liên hệ riêng tư; bài viết cần người lớn đánh giá.

examples: TASK · Describe a person OR a place at school, not both.
PERSON PLAN · My librarian → helps pupils → friendly → why I like her.
PLACE PLAN · School library → next to hall → books and tables → why I like it.
PLACE MODEL · My favourite place is our school library. It is next to the hall. There are many books and two large tables. I like it because I can read quietly with my friends.
PERSON MODEL · Mr Nam works in our school library. He helps students find books. He is patient and kind. I like him because he explains things clearly.
SELF-CHECK · Is every sentence about my chosen subject? Are the verbs and punctuation clear?

activities.prompt: The task asks you to describe ONE familiar person or place. Which plan follows the task?

options.text: Choose one subject, select relevant facts and note why you like it.
Describe both a person and a place even though the task asks for one.
Choose a person but use only unrelated details about a different event.
Choose a place but list names of other pupils instead of describing its features.

feedback.explanation_en: The task requires one chosen subject with relevant details and a personal reason. Mixing subjects or replacing its details with unrelated information does not fulfil the prompt.

activities.prompt: You chose to describe the school library. Which detail is relevant?

options.text: My uncle bought a bicycle yesterday.
The bus arrives in another city.
I forgot my sports shoes at home.

feedback.explanation_en: The tables tell the reader something concrete about the chosen place.

activities.prompt: Which outline gives the clearest order for a short description of one school place?

options.text: Opening → location → features → why I like it
Location → one feature → opening → why I like it
Opening → personal reason → unrelated holiday event → ending
Opening → place features → unrelated person → location

feedback.explanation_en: Start by introducing the same place, tell the reader where it is, develop its features and end with a reason. Other outlines delay the opening or interrupt the description with unrelated content.

activities.prompt: Choose the sentence with correct basic grammar for describing the school library.

options.text: There are many books in the library.
There is many books in the library.
There are a books in the library.
There are many book in the library.

feedback.explanation_en: Books is plural, so use there are and the plural noun books.

activities.prompt: Write one paragraph about EITHER a familiar person at school OR a place at school (real or imaginary). If you choose a person, explain who they are, what they do and why you like or appreciate them. If you choose a place, explain where it is, describe two features and say why you like it. Aim for about 40–60 words. Brainstorm three facts, make a short plan, then self-check your own paragraph. Do not include a private address, phone number or other personal contact details.

feedback.pending_message: Your paragraph is saved for adult review. Check the chosen subject and task details before revising; word count alone never determines your score.

lessons.title: Question words and basic question order
objectives: Choose who, what, where, when, why or how according to the information needed.
Ask simple present questions with do/does plus the base verb.
Invert be and the subject in be-questions.
Recognise when who is the subject and do/does is not added.

explanation.en: Question words help you ask for a specific kind of information: who (person), what (thing or activity), where (place), when (time), why (reason), how (method). With be, use question word + am/is/are + subject: Where is the library? With a normal present-simple verb, use question word + do/does + subject + base verb: When does the club meet? Who can be the subject itself: Who leads the club? Do not add does in that sentence. In a gap, type only the missing part.
explanation.vi: Who = ai, what = gì, where = ở đâu, when = khi nào, why = vì sao, how = như thế nào. Với be: Where is...; với động từ thường: Where does she go...? Sau does dùng động từ nguyên mẫu. Chỉ điền phần còn thiếu.

examples: PLACE · Where is the sports hall?
TIME · When does the club start?
REASON · Why are you late? Because the bus was slow.
METHOD · How do you get to school? By bus.
SUBJECT · Who teaches science? Ms Hoa.

activities.prompt: A student asks about the LOCATION of the art club. Choose the right question word. ___ is the club meeting?

feedback.explanation_en: Where asks for a place; when asks for a time.

activities.prompt: Complete the question about TIME. ___ does the bus leave? At eight o’clock. Enter one question word.

feedback.explanation_en: When asks about time. Do/does stays after the question word.

activities.prompt: Which question correctly asks about the person leading the club?

feedback.explanation_en: Who is the subject of leads; do/does is not needed in this subject question.

activities.prompt: Complete with the missing phrase only: Where ___ (your sister / study) after school?

feedback.explanation_en: With a singular subject, use does + subject + base verb study.

activities.prompt: Your friend says, “I am happy because I passed the quiz.” Which question asks for the REASON?

feedback.explanation_en: Why asks for a reason and because introduces one.

activities.prompt: Complete with ONE word: ___ is your science teacher? Ms Hoa.

feedback.explanation_en: Who asks about a person; is already printed in the question.

activities.prompt: Which question has correct word order?

feedback.explanation_en: With be, put is before the singular subject your classroom.

activities.prompt: Complete with one question word: ___ do you travel to school? By bus.

feedback.explanation_en: How asks about the way or method of travel.

activities.prompt: Which question asks about a thing or activity, NOT a person, time or place?

options.text: What do you do on Fridays?
Who do you meet on Fridays?

feedback.explanation_en: What asks for the activity; the other words ask for person, time or place.

activities.prompt: Complete the question with the missing phrase only: Why ___ (he / like) science?

feedback.explanation_en: A why-question in the present simple needs does + he + base verb like.

activities.prompt: At the art club, Linh helps Minh carry some paint. You want to ask which PERSON Linh helps (not who helps Linh). Select the question that asks for that person.

options.text: Who does Linh help at the art club?
Who helps Linh at the art club?
Who Linh helps at the art club?
Who does Linh helps at the art club?

feedback.explanation_en: Linh gives help and Minh receives it. To ask about the person Linh helps, use Who + does + Linh + base verb help. “Who helps Linh?” reverses who gives and receives help. Without inversion, “Who Linh helps...?” is not a complete direct question; after does, use help, not helps.

activities.prompt: Complete with the missing phrase ONLY: What ___ (your cousin / bring) to art club on Fridays?

feedback.explanation_en: Your cousin is third-person singular: does + subject + base verb bring.

activities.prompt: Your club leader wants to know the NUMBER of students in the chess club. Select one correctly formed question.

options.text: How much students are in the chess club?
How many student are in the chess club?
How many students are in the chess club?
How students many are in the chess club?

feedback.explanation_en: Use how many with the plural count noun students; invert are and the subject.

activities.prompt: Complete the yes/no question with the missing phrase ONLY: ___ (the library / close) at five?

feedback.explanation_en: The library is singular, so use Does + subject + base verb close.

lessons.title: Future intentions with be going to
objectives: Express a simple future intention using be going to plus a base verb.
Make negative statements and questions with the correct form of be.
Identify a prediction supported by visible evidence.
Distinguish a specific future plan from a regular habit.

explanation.en: Use am/is/are going to + base verb for an intention or plan: We are going to visit the museum. Put not after be for negatives: She is not going to come. Move be before the subject in questions: Are they going to join? A visible sign can also support a prediction: Those clouds are dark; it is going to rain. Compare the plan with a routine: We meet every Friday (habit), but we are going to meet on Saturday this week (plan). Do not use verb-ing after going to in this construction.
explanation.vi: Be going to + động từ nguyên mẫu: dự định hoặc dự đoán có căn cứ nhìn thấy. Chọn am/is/are theo chủ ngữ; phủ định đặt not sau be; câu hỏi đảo be lên trước chủ ngữ. Phân biệt thói quen với kế hoạch cụ thể.

examples: PLAN · I am going to learn a new song.
NEGATIVE · She is not going to take the bus.
QUESTION · Are you going to join us? Yes, I am.
EVIDENCE · Look at the dark clouds. It is going to rain.
CONTRAST · We usually walk, but today we are going to take the bus.

activities.prompt: I bought seeds yesterday and have a plan for Sunday. I ___ plant them in the school garden.

feedback.explanation_en: I takes am; be going to expresses the intended action.

activities.prompt: Complete the planned action: She ___ (be / going to / visit) her grandparents tomorrow. Enter only the missing phrase.

feedback.explanation_en: She takes is + going to + base verb visit.

activities.prompt: Which negative sentence correctly says the team has NO plan to travel by bus?

options.text: The team isn't going to travel by bus.
The team don't going to travel by bus.
The team isn't going travel by bus.
The team not going to travelling by bus.

feedback.explanation_en: Negative going to uses isn't/aren't + going to + base verb.

activities.prompt: Complete the question: ___ (you / going to / join) the science club next term?

feedback.explanation_en: Use Are + you + going to + base verb for a plan question.

activities.prompt: Look at those dark clouds. Choose a natural prediction based on what we can see.

feedback.explanation_en: Visible dark clouds support a going-to prediction; use is going to + base verb.

activities.prompt: Complete with the missing phrase only: We ___ (not / going to / buy) new chairs this month.

feedback.explanation_en: We takes are; the negative is aren't/are not going to + buy.

activities.prompt: Choose the correct short answer: Are they going to meet on Friday? (Yes.)

feedback.explanation_en: The auxiliary in the question is are, so use Yes, they are.

activities.prompt: Complete the question about intention with ONE word: What are you going to ___ after school?

feedback.explanation_en: After going to, use the base verb do.

activities.prompt: Which sentence describes a future plan rather than a usual routine?

options.text: We are going to meet next Tuesday.
We usually meet in the library.
We meet on most school days.

feedback.explanation_en: Be going to expresses the specific future intention; the other choices express habits.

activities.prompt: Complete: My brother ___ (be / going to / make) a poster this evening.

feedback.explanation_en: My brother is singular; use is going to make.

activities.prompt: Maya has decided to make a poster at home tomorrow, but she has not arranged a meeting with anyone. Select one sentence that expresses HER INTENTION.

options.text: Maya makes a poster every Friday.
Maya is going to make a poster tomorrow.
Maya has made a poster already.

feedback.explanation_en: Be going to describes Maya’s previously decided future intention; the other options report past actions or a routine.

activities.prompt: The team has changed its plan. Complete with the missing phrase ONLY: They ___ (be / not / going to / use) the old classroom next week.

feedback.explanation_en: The plural subject they takes are; negate be before going to, then use the base verb.

activities.prompt: The school has CONFIRMED an appointment with the photographer for Friday at nine. Select one sentence that uses the PRESENT CONTINUOUS for this fixed future arrangement.

options.text: We meet the photographer every Friday.
We are meeting the photographer at nine on Friday.
We meeting the photographer at nine on Friday.
We were meeting the photographer yesterday.

feedback.explanation_en: Are meeting is present continuous and can express a confirmed future arrangement. A describes a habit; C omits are; D describes the past.

activities.prompt: A heavy branch is bending in strong wind. Complete the prediction with the missing phrase ONLY: That branch ___ (be / going to / fall)!

feedback.explanation_en: Visible evidence supports a be going to prediction; that branch takes is.

lessons.title: Rules: must, must not and have to
objectives: Identify required, forbidden and optional actions from everyday notices.
Use must and must not with a base verb.
Use have to/has to and do/does not have to with correct agreement.
Ask about necessity with do/does + have to.

explanation.en: Must + base verb expresses an obligation: You must wear a helmet. Must not (mustn’t) expresses prohibition: You mustn’t enter. Have to/has to also expresses a requirement: She has to bring her card. Do not have to means an action is not necessary, NOT forbidden: You don’t have to bring paper; the club provides it. To ask about necessity, use Do we have to bring a notebook? or Does she have to register? After must and have to, use the base verb. Read the notice carefully to decide whether a rule requires, forbids or merely makes something optional.
explanation.vi: Must/have to = bắt buộc; mustn’t = cấm; don’t have to = không bắt buộc (vẫn có thể làm). He/she/it dùng has to, câu hỏi dùng does ... have to. Không nhầm cấm với không cần.

examples: REQUIRED · You must wear safety glasses.
FORBIDDEN · You mustn’t run in the corridor.
OPTIONAL · You don’t have to bring paper.
AGREEMENT · She has to show her card.
QUESTION · Do we have to book a place?

activities.prompt: The laboratory rule says students must wear safety glasses. Which sentence expresses an OBLIGATION?

options.text: Students must not wear safety glasses.
Students do not have to wear safety glasses.

feedback.explanation_en: Must wear expresses the required action. Must not means prohibited; do not have to means optional.

activities.prompt: Complete with the missing expression of prohibition: You ___ touch the chemicals without a teacher.

feedback.explanation_en: Must not/mustn’t prohibits the action, rather than making it optional.

activities.prompt: The art club provides paper; bringing paper is OPTIONAL. Which sentence matches?

options.text: You do not have to bring paper.

feedback.explanation_en: Do not have to = not necessary, not prohibited.

activities.prompt: Complete: We ___ (have to / arrive) before 9 a.m. for registration. Enter only the missing phrase.

feedback.explanation_en: We have to arrive states the requirement; use the base verb after have to.

activities.prompt: Which question asks whether joining the event is necessary?

options.text: Do we have to join the event?
Have we to joins the event?
Must we to join the event?
Do we must join the event?

feedback.explanation_en: Use Do + subject + have to + base verb to ask about necessity.

activities.prompt: Complete with ONE word: She ___ to bring her student card every day.

feedback.explanation_en: She has to, not have to, in an affirmative statement.

activities.prompt: The notice says “No running in the corridor.” Choose the matching rule.

options.text: You do not have to run in the corridor.
You must not run in the corridor.
You have to run in the corridor.
You must run in the corridor.

feedback.explanation_en: Must not describes a prohibited action.

activities.prompt: Complete: The trip is free. You ___ (not / have to / pay) a fee. Enter only the missing phrase.

feedback.explanation_en: Do not have to pay means payment is not required; it does not ban paying for something else.

activities.prompt: Which sentence is grammatical and expresses a school requirement?

options.text: He has to show his card.
He have to showing his card.
He must to show his card.
He does has to show his card.

feedback.explanation_en: He has to + base verb is the correct affirmative form.

activities.prompt: Complete the negative rule with the missing phrase only: Visitors ___ (must / not / enter) this room.

feedback.explanation_en: Must not/mustn't + base verb states a prohibition.

activities.prompt: Museum visitors may take photographs, but flash photography is FORBIDDEN. Select one sentence that matches the rule.

options.text: Visitors do not have to use flash.

feedback.explanation_en: Must not states a prohibition. Do not have to only means there is no obligation, not that something is forbidden.

activities.prompt: The art club supplies paintbrushes. Complete with the missing phrase ONLY: Liam ___ (not / have to / bring) a paintbrush.

feedback.explanation_en: Not necessary is expressed by does not have to; after does, use have rather than has.

activities.prompt: Trip instructions say: arriving by 8:00 is compulsory; bringing lunch is optional because lunch is provided. Select one sentence that expresses BOTH rules correctly.

options.text: We must not arrive by eight, and we have to bring lunch.
We do not have to arrive by eight, and we must bring lunch.
We have to arrive by eight, and we do not have to bring lunch.
We have to arrive by eight, and we must not bring lunch.

feedback.explanation_en: Have to marks the required arrival; do not have to marks the optional lunch. Optional does not mean forbidden.

activities.prompt: Complete the question with the missing phrase ONLY: ___ (she / have to / wear) a badge to enter the library?

feedback.explanation_en: Questions with have to take does + subject + have to + base verb.

lessons.title: Family, rooms and everyday belongings
objectives: Understand common family relationships from short statements.
Recognise the purpose of basic rooms and household objects.
Use common family and home words in short natural phrases.
Avoid making assumptions about a relative’s age or home.

explanation.en: Learn family words by relationships: your mother’s sister is your aunt; your father’s brother is your uncle; your aunt’s child is your cousin. Grandparents are your parents’ parents. At home, a kitchen is for preparing food and a bedroom has a bed. Learn words in useful phrases: visit my grandparents, tidy my room, put plates in the kitchen. A cousin is a relative, but the word does not tell you their age or where they live.
explanation.vi: Học theo quan hệ: aunt = cô/dì/bác gái; uncle = chú/cậu/bác trai; cousin = anh/chị/em họ; grandparents = ông bà. Học từ theo cụm dùng được trong đời thường; đừng suy đoán tuổi hay nơi ở chỉ từ quan hệ.

examples: FAMILY · My aunt is my mother’s sister.
RELATION · My cousin is my aunt’s child.
VISIT · I visit my grandparents on Sundays.
ROOM · We prepare dinner in the kitchen.
BEDROOM · There is a pillow on my bed.

activities.prompt: My mother’s sister is my ___.

feedback.explanation_en: Aunt can mean the sister of a parent.

activities.prompt: Complete: My father’s brother is my ___. Enter one family word.

feedback.explanation_en: A brother of a parent is an uncle.

activities.prompt: Where do you normally prepare a meal at home?

feedback.explanation_en: The kitchen is the room used for preparing food.

activities.prompt: My cousin is my aunt’s child. Which statement must be true?

options.text: We live in the same house.

feedback.explanation_en: A cousin is a family relation; age, home and school are not determined.

activities.prompt: Complete: Please put the clean plates in the ___. (room for cooking)

feedback.explanation_en: The kitchen is a room for preparing food.

explanation.en: A changed plan often contains both old and new information. Highlight the new venue, the new start time and any earlier arrival time. Read if-clauses carefully: if you have no T-shirt, a spare is available; if you already replied, you only need to reply again when your plans change.
